```
Google Colab does not offer an official public API, meaning programmatic control over notebooks must rely on managing files via the Google Drive API or reverse-engineering Colab's web architecture. [1, 2, 3] 

If you are looking to automate, reverse engineer, or interact directly with the Google Colab web environment, the system is fundamentally structured around a custom reverse proxy and local Jupyter socket layers.

The Core Architecture of Colab Web Requests

Security researchers poking "behind the curtain" of Google Colab have mapped out the distinct sub-components that manage code execution and file tracking: [4, 5] 

The Reverse Proxy: Colab uses an internal reverse proxy to communicate with the standard Jupyter socket running on the allocated remote virtual machine. [5] 

Key Intercept Endpoints: When looking at the browser's Network tab (F12), the primary WebSocket and data endpoints handling notebook updates and file transfers include:

/socket.io — Handles live WebSocket communication, cell executions, and real-time state sync.

/files — Manages runtime local storage and directories.

/api/contents — Used for fetching and writing notebook components. [5, 6] 

The Backend Loop: The virtual machine spins up a NodeJS application (node) alongside a custom jupyter-notebook process listening internally on port 9000. [5] 

Common Strategies for Automation

Because Google actively guards against automated abuse (like headless bot farming of their free GPUs), direct raw HTTP replay attacks fail quickly due to dynamic anti-bot signatures and cookie rotations. Developers use alternative reverse-engineering approaches: [7, 8, 9, 10] 

In-Context Session Scripts: Instead of writing raw requests or fetch scripts from the outside, automated extensions run directly within an active, human-authenticated browser session. This allows scripts to use the browser’s existing authentication headers, origin context, and active cookies seamlessly. [7] 

Exposing the Internal Runtime: To run workloads without sitting on the frontend webpage, developers bypass the UI entirely by injecting an SSH layer into the active notebook session. Services like Cloudflare Tunnels or ngrok are script-injected to expose the underlying Python environment as a private API endpoint. [4, 10, 11] 

File Syncing via Drive API: If your target is reading notebook outputs or writing code to run later, treating Colab notebooks purely as .ipynb files inside Google Drive allows you to use Google's official Drive SDK rather than hacking frontend web selectors. [1]
```

```
While Google actively blocks raw standalone scripts that try to farm or simulate web traffic via pure HTTP requests, several reverse-engineered frameworks, official hybrid workarounds, and scripting patterns are available to interact with Colab programmatically.

Existing code and automation approaches fall into three main tiers:

1. In-Browser JavaScript Reverse Engineering (Tampermonkey / Console)

Because Colab relies heavily on standard WebSockets (/socket.io) and internal Jupyter APIs (/api/contents), developers use browser-context scripts to bypass Google's anti-bot protections entirely. These scripts execute natively using your pre-authenticated session cookies. [1] 

Automated Cell Execution & Keep-Alive Snippet:
This script simulates user interaction directly in the DOM to click the "Connect" button, prevent idle timeouts, and execute cells.

// Paste into the Browser F12 Console or use as a Tampermonkey script function ClickConnect() { console.log("Checking for Connection/Timeout prompts..."); // Target the toolbar connect button let connectBtn = document.querySelector("#connect-button") || document.querySelector("colab-connect-button"); if (connectBtn && connectBtn.shadowRoot) { let actualBtn = connectBtn.shadowRoot.querySelector("#connect"); if (actualBtn && actualBtn.textContent.includes("Connect")) { actualBtn.click(); console.log("Clicked Connect Button!"); } } // Auto-dismiss the "Are you still there?" dialog box let dialogBtn = document.querySelector("#ok"); if (dialogBtn) { dialogBtn.click(); console.log("Dismissed the idle dialog box."); } } // Run every 60 seconds setInterval(ClickConnect, 60000); 

2. Official Extensions (VS Code Integration)

Google has opened up an internal, official bridging API that connects external IDEs directly to the hosted Colab kernel. [2, 3] 

The Google Colab VS Code Extension: Available in the VS Code Marketplace.

How it works: It establishes an authenticated OAuth tunnel directly to Google’s internal backend runtime manager. By selecting "Colab" as your remote Jupyter Kernel inside VS Code, you can trigger execution, manage files, and automate pipelines using local Python execution wrappers.

3. Exposing Colab as a Remote Worker API (Python Inversion)

Instead of trying to push commands into Colab from the outside, the most reliable "reverse" pattern forces Colab to reach out and pull workloads using tunnel code. [4, 5] 

By installing an SSH layer or an API proxy like Ollama or Text-Generation-WebUI inside the Colab instance, you can use a tunnel tool like ngrok or Cloudflare to treat your free GPU instance as a live web server API endpoint.
```

```
ion_store"), f"{session_id}.json")

uests.Session:

ions, dict):

def solve_pow(challenge: dict) -> str:
    inp = json.dumps(challenge)
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["node", str(WASM_SOLVER)],
            input=inp,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"POW solver error: {proc.st
derr.strip()}")
        answer = int(proc.stdout.strip())
    except Exception as e:
        console.print(f"[red]POW solving failed: {e}[/]")
        sys.exit(1)

    payload = {
        "algorithm": challenge.get("algorithm", "DeepSeekHa
shV1"),
        "challenge": challenge["challenge"],
        "salt": challenge["salt"],
        "answer": answer,
        "signature": challenge["signature"],
        "target_path": challenge.get("target_path", "/api/v
0/chat/completion")
    }
    return base64.b64encode(json.dumps(payload).encode()).d
ecode()
```

```bash
import os, json, yaml
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict

class SessionManager:
    def __init__(self, config_path=None):
        if config_path is None:
            config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "config.yaml"
        self.config = {}
        if Path(config_path).exists():
            with open(config_path) as f:
                self.config = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}

    def get(self, provider: str, key: str, default=None) -> Any:
        # environment override for token paths
        env_map = {
            "deepseek_token_path": "DEEPSEEK_TOKEN_PATH",
            "mistral_token_path": "MISTRAL_TOKEN_PATH",
            "claude_token_path": "CLAUDE_TOKEN_PATH",
            "gemini_token_path": "GEMINI_TOKEN_PATH",
            "colab_token_path": "COLAB_TOKEN_PATH",
        }
        env_key = f"{provider}_{key}"
        if env_key in env_map and os.getenv(env_map[env_key]):
            return os.getenv(env_map[env_key])
        # fallback to config file
        return self.config.get(provider, {}).get(key, default)

    def get_token(self, provider: str) -> str:
        """Read token from file or return None."""
        token_path = self.get(provider, "token_path")
        if token_path:
            expanded = os.path.expanduser(token_path)
            if os.path.exists(expanded):
                with open(expanded) as f:
                    return f.read().strip()

from pathlib import Path
from curl_cffi import requests as curl_requests
from .base import ChatBackend

BASE_URL = "https://chat.deepseek.com"
WASM_SOLVER = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "deepcli" / "pow_solver.js"
# fallback location
if not WASM_SOLVER.exists():
    WASM_SOLVER = Path.home() / "deepcli" / "pow_solver.js"

class DeepSeekBackend(ChatBackend):
    def __init__(self, session_manager):
        self.token = session_manager.get_token("deepseek")
        if not self.token:
            # try env
            self.token = os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_TOKEN")
        if not self.token:
            # try harmony_hub style
            try:
                sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.home() / "harmony_hub"))
                from src.token_provider_v2 import get_token
                self.token = get_token("primary")
            except: pass
        self.cookie = None
        cookie_path = session_manager.get("deepseek", "cookie_path")
        if cookie_path and os.path.exists(os.path.expanduser(cookie_path)):
            with open(os.path.expanduser(cookie_path)) as f:
                cookies = json.load(f)
            for c in cookies:
                if c.get("name") == "ds_session_id":
                    self.cookie = c.get("value")
                    break
        self._session = None

    def is_available(self):
        return bool(self.token)

    def _get_session(self):
        if self._session is None:
            s = curl_requests.Session()
            s.headers.update({
                "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:134.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/134.0",
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}",
                "X-Client-Platform": "web",
                "X-Client-Version": "1.3.0-auto-resume",
                "X-App-Version": "20241129.1",
                "X-Client-Locale": "en_US",
                "Origin": BASE_URL,
                "Referer": f"{BASE_URL}/",
            })
            if self.cookie:
                s.cookies.set("ds_session_id", self.cookie)
            self._session = s
        return self._session

    def solve_pow(self, challenge: dict) -> str:
        inp = json.dumps(challenge)
        proc = subprocess.run(["node", str(WASM_SOLVER)], input=inp,
                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"POW error: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
        answer = int(proc.stdout.strip())
        payload = {
            "algorithm": challenge.get("algorithm", "DeepSeekHashV1"),
            "challenge": challenge["challenge"],
            "salt": challenge["salt"],
            "answer": answer,
            "signature": challenge["signature"],
            "target_path": challenge.get("target_path", "/api/v0/chat/completion")
        }
        return base64.b64encode(json.dumps(payload).encode()).decode()

    def get_pow_challenge(self):
        s = self._get_session()
        r = s.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v0/chat/create_pow_challenge",
                   json={"target_path": "/api/v0/chat/completion"})
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["data"]["biz_data"]["challenge"]

    def create_session(self, model_type="expert"):
        s = self._get_session()
        r = s.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v0/chat_session/create",
                   json={"character_id": None, "model_type": model_type})
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["data"]["biz_data"]["id"]

    def send_message(self, message: str, context: list[dict]) -> str:
        challenge = self.get_pow_challenge()
        pow_header = self.solve_pow(challenge)
        # need a chat_session; create one or reuse from context metadata
        session_id = None
        if context and "__session_id" in context[0]:
            session_id = context[0]["__session_id"]
        else:
            session_id = self.create_session()
            # store in metadata
            context.insert(0, {"role": "meta", "__session_id": session_id})

        payload = {
            "chat_session_id": session_id,
            "parent_message_id": None,
            "prompt": message,
            "ref_file_ids": [],
            "thinking_enabled": True,
            "search_enabled": False,
            "stream": False,
        }
        s = self._get_session()
        headers = s.headers.copy()
        headers["X-Ds-Pow-Response"] = pow_header
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        resp = curl_requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v0/chat/completion",
                                 json=payload, headers=headers)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json()
        return data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

class ChatDispatcher:
    def __init__(self, mgr: SessionManager):
        self.mgr = mgr
        self.instances = {}

    def get_backend(self, name):
        if name not in self.instances:
            cls = BACKENDS.get(name)
            if not cls:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown backend: {name}")
            self.instances[name] = cls(self.mgr)
        inst = self.instances[name]
        if not inst.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError(f"Backend '{name}' is not available. Check token/cookies.")
        return inst

    def send(self, provider, message, session_id=None):
        backend = self.get_backend(provider)
        context = []
        if session_id:
            context = cache_load(session_id) or []
        reply = backend.send_message(message, context)
        if session_id:
            context.append({"role": "user", "content": message})
            context.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
            cache_save(session_id, context)
        return reply

const { chromium } = require('playwright-core');  // lighter than puppeteer
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const COOKIES_FILE = process.argv[2] || path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '.multi-ai-tokens', 'mistral_cookies.json');
const TOKEN_FILE = process.argv[2] ? process.argv[3] : path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '.multi-ai-tokens', 'mistral_token.txt');

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: false, args: ['--no-sandbox'] });
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();

  // Load saved cookies if available
  if (fs.existsSync(COOKIES_FILE)) {
    const cookies = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(COOKIES_FILE));
    await context.addCookies(cookies);
  }

  let capturedToken = null;
  page.on('request', req => {
    const auth = req.headers()['authorization'];
    if (auth && auth.startsWith('Bearer ') && !capturedToken) {
      capturedToken = auth.replace('Bearer ', '');
      console.log('🔥 Captured Mistral token!');
    }
  });

  await page.goto('https://chat.mistral.ai', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
  console.log('👉 Please log in manually, then press Enter in this terminal...');
  process.stdin.once('data', async () => {
    // Navigate to trigger API calls
    await page.goto('https://chat.mistral.ai', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
    await page.waitForTimeout(3000);

    // Save cookies
    const cookies = await context.cookies();
    fs.writeFileSync(COOKIES_FILE, JSON.stringify(cookies, null, 2));
    console.log('🍪 Cookies saved.');

    if (capturedToken) {
      fs.writeFileSync(TOKEN_FILE, capturedToken);
      console.log('✅ Token saved to', TOKEN_FILE);
    } else {
      console.log('❌ No token captured. Run again and try interacting with the page.');
    }
    await browser.close();
    process.exit(0);
  });
})();
```

```bash
        if self._session is None:

            s.headers.update({
```

```bash
class DeepSeekBackend(ChatBackend):
    def __init__(self, session_manager):
        # token
        self.token = session_manager.get_token("deepseek")
        if not self.token:
            self.token = os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_TOKEN")
        if not self.token:

                from src.token_provider_v2 import get_token
                self.token = get_token("primary")
            except: pass

        # cookie
        self.cookie = None
        cookie_path = session_manager.get("deepseek", "cookie_path")
        if cookie_path:
            cp = os.path.expanduser(cookie_path)
            if os.path.exists(cp):
                with open(cp) as f:
                    data = json.load(f)
                cookies = data if isinstance(data, list) else data.get('cookies', [])
                for c in cookies:
                    if c.get("name") == "ds_session_id":
                        self.cookie = c.get("value")
                        break
        self._session = None

    def is_available(self):
        return bool(self.token)

    def _get_session(self):
        if self._session is None:
            s = curl_requests.Session()
            s.headers.update({
                "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:134.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/134.0",
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}",
                "X-Client-Platform": "web",
                "X-Client-Version": "1.3.0-auto-resume",
                "X-App-Version": "20241129.1",
                "X-Client-Locale": "en_US",
                "Origin": BASE_URL,
                "Referer": f"{BASE_URL}/",
            })
            if self.cookie:
                s.cookies.set("ds_session_id", self.cookie)
            self._session = s
        return self._session

    def solve_pow(self, challenge: dict) -> str:
        inp = json.dumps(challenge)
        proc = subprocess.run(["node", str(WASM_SOLVER)], input=inp,
                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"POW error: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
        answer = int(proc.stdout.strip())
        payload = {
            "algorithm": challenge.get("algorithm", "DeepSeekHashV1"),
            "challenge": challenge["challenge"],
            "salt": challenge["salt"],
            "answer": answer,
            "signature": challenge["signature"],
            "target_path": challenge.get("target_path", "/api/v0/chat/completion")
        }
        return base64.b64encode(json.dumps(payload).encode()).decode()

    def get_pow_challenge(self):
        s = self._get_session()
        r = s.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v0/chat/create_pow_challenge",
                   json={"target_path": "/api/v0/chat/completion"})
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["data"]["biz_data"]["challenge"]

    def create_session(self, model_type="expert"):
        s = self._get_session()
        r = s.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v0/chat_session/create",
                   json={"character_id": None, "model_type": model_type})
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["data"]["biz_data"]["id"]

    def send_message(self, message: str, context: list[dict]) -> str:
        challenge = self.get_pow_challenge()
        pow_header = self.solve_pow(challenge)

        # reuse or create session id
        session_id = None
        for m in context:
            if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("__session_id"):
                session_id = m["__session_id"]
                break
        if not session_id:
            session_id = self.create_session()
            context.insert(0, {"role": "meta", "__session_id": session_id})

        payload = {
            "chat_session_id": session_id,
            "parent_message_id": None,
            "prompt": message,
            "ref_file_ids": [],
            "thinking_enabled": True,
            "search_enabled": False,
            "stream": False,  # server ignores this, always SSE

        s = self._get_session()
        headers = s.headers.copy()
        headers["X-Ds-Pow-Response"] = pow_header
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

        resp = curl_requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/v0/chat/completion",
            json=payload,
            headers=headers,
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()

        # --- parse SSE manually (server always streams) ---
        final_content = ""
        for line in resp.text.split("\n"):

                    # The "v" object contains the actual message chunk
                    if isinstance(data, dict) and "v" in data:

                        if isinstance(data, dict) and "content" in data:
                            final_content += data["content"]
                    except:
                        pass

        return final_content if final_content else "[No content returned]"
```

```
def _complete_file_path(text, state):
    """Tab-complete file paths for /attach."""
    if not text.startswith('/') and not text.startswith('~') and not text.startswith('.'):
        text = './' + text
    expanded = os.path.expanduser(text)
    matches = _glob.glob(expanded + '*')
    try:
        return matches[state]
    except IndexError:
        return None

def _smart_completer(text, state):
    buf = readline.get_line_buffer()
    if buf.lstrip().startswith('/attach'):
        parts = buf.split()
        if len(parts) >= 2 and not buf.endswith(' '):
            return _complete_file_path(parts[-1], state)
    if _original_completer:
        return _original_completer(text, state)
    return None

MAX_TREE_LINES = 200

def build_tree_str(messages, selected_parent_id=None, max_depth=8, content_width=50, max_lines=200):
    total_lines = 0  # nonlocal in _render
    lines = []
    msg_map = {}
    for m in messages:
        m["_children"] = []
        msg_map[m["message_id"]] = m
    roots = []
    for m in messages:
        pid = m.get("parent_id")
        if pid and pid in msg_map:
            msg_map[pid]["_children"].append(m)
        else:
            roots.append(m)

    def _render(node, prefix="", is_last=False, depth=0):
        nonlocal total_lines
        if depth > max_depth or total_lines >= max_lines:
            if total_lines == max_lines:
                lines.append("[yellow](output truncated, /more to see full tree)[/]")
            total_lines += 1
            return
        role = node.get("role","").upper()
        mid = node.get("message_id")
        content = node.get("content","")[:content_width].replace("\n"," ")
        marker = "🔽 " if mid == selected_parent_id else ""
        connector = "└── " if is_last else "├── " if prefix else ""
        if role == "USER":
            lines.append(f"{prefix}{connector}[blue]{marker}👤 [{mid}] {content}[/]")
        else:
            lines.append(f"{prefix}{connector}[green]{marker}🤖 [{mid}] {content}[/]")
        total_lines += 1
        children = node.get("_children",[])
        for i, child in enumerate(children):
            last = (i == len(children)-1)
            new_prefix = prefix + ("   " if is_last else "│  ")
            _render(child, new_prefix, last, depth+1)

    for r in roots:
        _render(r)
    return "\n".join(lines)

def choose_message(messages, role_filter=None, label=""):
    """Pick a message, optionally filtered by role."""
    candidates = messages
    if role_filter:
        candidates = [m for m in messages if m.get("role","").upper() == role_filter.upper()]
    if not candidates:
        console.print(f"[red]No {label} messages found.[/]")
        return None
    console.print(f"[bold]Select a {label} message:[/]")
    for i, m in enumerate(candidates):
        snippet = (m.get("content","")[:60]).replace("\n"," ")
        emoji = "👤" if m.get("role","").upper() == "USER" else "🤖"
        console.print(f"  [{i}] {emoji} {snippet}")
    console.print("  [c] cancel")
    choice = input("Choice (number or c): ").strip()
    if choice.lower() == 'c':
        return None
    try:
        idx = int(choice)
        if 0 <= idx < len(candidates):
            return candidates[idx]["message_id"]
    except:
        pass
    return None


def browse_sessions(_=''):
    """Interactive session browser with real‑time category toggles."""
    # ── load all sessions with metadata ──
    all_sessions = []
    cache_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/.deepcli/session_store')
    if os.path.isdir(cache_dir):
        for f in Path(cache_dir).glob('*.json'):
            try:
                data = json.loads(f.read_text())
                msgs = data if isinstance(data, list) else data.get('messages', [])
                if msgs:
                    first = msgs[0].get('content','')[:100] if isinstance(msgs[0], dict) else str(msgs[0])[:100]
                    # auto‑detect project
                    proj = 'general'
                    for pj, keys in {'archwiz':['archwiz','cockpit','dashboard'],
                                     'deepcli':['deepcli','core.py','tui.py'],
                                     'synthegration':['synthegration','branch_manager'],
                                     'harmony_hub':['harmony_hub','token_provider'],
                                     'multi-agent':['multi-agent','orchestrator'],
                                     'cedar':['cedrlang','compression protocol'],
                                     'caveman':['caveman','disk cleanup']}.items():
                        if any(k in first.lower() for k in keys): proj = pj; break
                    is_agent = 'agent' in first.lower() or 'task' in first.lower()
                    is_test = 'test' in f.stem or 'echo' in first.lower() or len(msgs) <= 2
                    all_sessions.append({'sid':f.stem, 'msgs':len(msgs), 'snippet':first,
                                         'mtime':f.stat().st_mtime, 'proj':proj,
                                         'agent':is_agent, 'test':is_test})
            except: pass
    all_sessions.sort(key=lambda x: x['mtime'], reverse=True)

    # ── filter state ──
    show_agent = True; show_test = True; show_human = True
    proj_filter = None  # None = all
    projects = sorted(set(s['proj'] for s in all_sessions))
    per_page = 15; page = 0
    project_idx = 0  # which project is selected in the filter

    def filtered():
        return [s for s in all_sessions
                if (show_agent or not s['agent'])
                and (show_test or not s['test'])
                and (show_human or (s['agent'] or s['test']))
                and (proj_filter is None or s['proj'] == proj_filter)]

    while True:
        f = filtered()
        total = len(f)
        start = page * per_page
        page_sessions = f[start:start+per_page]

        console.clear()
        console.print(f"[bold]📂 Session Explorer – {total} sessions[/]")
        # ── filter bar ──
        agent_str = f"[{'green' if show_agent else 'red'}](A)gent[/]"
        test_str = f"[{'green' if show_test else 'red'}](T)est[/]"
        human_str = f"[{'green' if show_human else 'red'}](H)uman[/]"
        proj_str = f"[cyan](P)roject: {proj_filter or 'all'}[/]"
        console.print(f"  {agent_str}  {test_str}  {human_str}  {proj_str}  [dim]c=clear[/]")
        console.print("─" * 60)

        for i, s in enumerate(page_sessions):
            ts = datetime.fromtimestamp(s['mtime']).strftime('%m-%d %H:%M')
            tags = []
            if s['agent']: tags.append('A')
            if s['test']: tags.append('T')
            tag_str = f" [yellow]{','.join(tags)}[/]" if tags else ""
            console.print(f"  [yellow]{start+i:3d}[/] {s['sid'][:12]}... [dim]({s['msgs']} msgs, {ts})[/] [{s['proj']}]{tag_str} {s['snippet'][:50]}")

        console.print("─" * 60)
        console.print("[dim]n=next, p=prev, A/T/H=toggle, P=cycle project, c=clear filters, q=quit[/]")
        cmd = input("> ").strip().lower()
        if cmd == 'n' and (start+per_page) < total: page += 1
        elif cmd == 'p' and page > 0: page -= 1
        elif cmd == 'q': break
        elif cmd == 'a': show_agent = not show_agent; page = 0
        elif cmd == 't': show_test = not show_test; page = 0
        elif cmd == 'h': show_human = not show_human; page = 0
        elif cmd == 'c': show_agent=show_test=show_human=True; proj_filter=None; page=0
        elif cmd == 'p' and projects:
            project_idx = (project_idx + 1) % len(projects)
            proj_filter = projects[project_idx]; page = 0
        else: pass

def prompt_session_id():
    token = get_token()

        sessions = fetch_sessions(token)
    except Exception:
        sessions = []

    if sessions:
        console.print("[bold]Recent sessions:[/]")
        table = Table(show_header=False, box=None)
        table.add_column("Num", style="bold")
        table.add_column("Title")
        table.add_column("ID", style="dim")
        for i, s in enumerate(sessions):
            sid = s.get("id") or s.get("chat_session_id")
            title = s.get("title") or s.get("name") or "(untitled)"
            table.add_row(f"[{i}]", title[:50], sid[:8] + "...")
        console.print(table)
        console.print("  [n] New session")
    else:
        console.print("No existing sessions. Creating a new one.")

    while True:
        choice = input("Select number or /new (or /help): ").strip()
        if choice.lower() in ['n', '/new']:
            return ('new', 'instant')
        if choice.lower() == '/help':
            console.print("[bold]At this stage:[/] enter a number to pick a session, or /new to start a new one.")
            continue
        if choice.lower().startswith('/browse'):
            browse_sessions(choice[7:].strip())
            continue
        if choice.lower() in ['/quit', '/exit']:
            console.print(random.choice(GOODBYES))
            sys.exit(0)
        if sessions:
            try:
                idx = int(choice)
                if 0 <= idx < len(sessions):
                    sel = sessions[idx]
                    sid = sel.get("id") or sel.get("chat_session_id")
                    mt = sel.get("model_type", "default")
                    mode = "expert" if mt == "expert" else "instant"
                    return (sid, mode)
            except:
                pass
        console.print("[red]Invalid choice.[/]")
```

## 4. Mistral Backend (cookie-first, zero deps)

Based on your existing `deepseek.py` pattern and Mistral’s known web structure, the web app sends requests to `https://chat.mistral.ai/api/chat` with a session cookie (`__Secure-next-auth.session-token` or similar). We can use cookies from your Firefox bookmarklet export. Paste this into sandbox:

```bash
cat > ~/multi-ai-cli/sandbox/backends/mistral_v1.py << 'PYEOF'
import os, json
from pathlib import Path
from curl_cffi import requests as curl_requests
# No mistralai SDK — pure HTTP like your DeepSeek backend

COOKIE_FILE = Path.home() / ".multi-ai-tokens" / "mistral_cookies.json"
TOKEN_FILE = Path.home() / ".multi-ai-tokens" / "mistral_token.txt"
BASE = "https://chat.mistral.ai"

class MistralV1Backend:
    def __init__(self):
        self.session = curl_requests.Session()
        self.token = None
        # Load token if exists (future use)
        if TOKEN_FILE.exists():
            self.token = TOKEN_FILE.read_text().strip()
            self.session.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self.token}"
        # Load cookies (from bookmarklet export)
        if COOKIE_FILE.exists():
            with open(COOKIE_FILE) as f:
                cookies = json.load(f)
            if isinstance(cookies, list):
                for c in cookies:
                    self.session.cookies.set(
                        c["name"], c["value"],
                        domain=c.get("domain", ".mistral.ai"),
                        path=c.get("path", "/")
                    )
            elif isinstance(cookies, dict) and "cookies" in cookies:
                for c in cookies["cookies"]:
                    self.session.cookies.set(c["name"], c["value"],
                                            domain=c.get("domain", ".mistral.ai"))
        self.session.headers.update({
            "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux aarch64) AppleWebKit/537.36",
            "Origin": BASE,
            "Referer": f"{BASE}/",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        })

    def is_available(self):
        # Test by hitting the session endpoint
        try:
            r = self.session.get(f"{BASE}/api/auth/session")
            return r.status_code == 200 and "user" in r.text.lower()
        except:
            return False

    def send_message(self, message: str, context: list) -> str:
        # Build messages array
        msgs = []
        for m in context:
            if m["role"] in ("user", "assistant"):
                msgs.append({"role": m["role"], "content": m["content"]})
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": message})

        payload = {
            "messages": msgs,
            "model": "mistral-large-latest",
            "temperature": 0.7,
        }
        # Mistral's web chat endpoint (observed from network tab)
        r = self.session.post(f"{BASE}/api/chat/completions", json=payload)
        if r.status_code != 200:
            # Fallback: older endpoint
            r = self.session.post(f"{BASE}/api/chat", json=payload)
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()
        # Extract reply
        if "choices" in data:
            return data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
        elif "content" in data:
            return data["content"]
        else:
            return json.dumps(data)

# Make a module-level instance for the promotion test
backend = MistralV1Backend()
PYEOF
```

```bash
const path = require('path');

const OUT = path.join(process.env.HOME, '.multi-ai-tokens', 'mistral_cookies.json');

(async () => {
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract cookies from Chromium profile for mistral.ai domain."""
import sqlite3, json, os, shutil
from pathlib import Path

COOKIE_DB = Path.home() / "browser-data-mistral" / "Default" / "Cookies"
OUT = Path.home() / ".multi-ai-tokens" / "mistral_cookies.json"
TOKEN_OUT = Path.home() / ".multi-ai-tokens" / "mistral_token.txt"

if not COOKIE_DB.exists():
    print(f"Cookie database not found at {COOKIE_DB}")
    print("Launch Chromium first with: ~/multi-ai-cli/harvesters/launch-mistral.sh")
    exit(1)

# Chromium locks the DB while running; copy to temp
tmp_db = "/tmp/mistral_cookies_tmp.db"
shutil.copy2(COOKIE_DB, tmp_db)

conn = sqlite3.connect(tmp_db)
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
cookies = []
for row in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM cookies WHERE host_key LIKE '%mistral%'"):
    cookies.append({
        "name": row["name"],
        "value": row["encrypted_value"] if row["encrypted_value"] else row["value"],
        "domain": row["host_key"],
        "path": row["path"],
        "expires": row["expires_utc"],
        "httpOnly": bool(row["is_httponly"]),
        "secure": bool(row["is_secure"]),
    })
conn.close()
os.unlink(tmp_db)

with open(OUT, "w") as f:
    json.dump(cookies, f, indent=2)
print(f"Extracted {len(cookies)} Mistral cookies → {OUT}")

# Also try to find an auth token in cookies
for c in cookies:
    if c["name"] in ("session", "token", "__Secure-next-auth.session-token", "next-auth.session-token"):
        TOKEN_OUT.write_text(c["value"])
        print(f"Auth token saved → {TOKEN_OUT}")
        break
else:
    print("No obvious auth token cookie found; may need to intercept Bearer header.")
    print("Try sending a chat via the browser, then re-extract cookies.")
PYEOF
```

content: What about Termux X11 in Android with Accessibility enabled?

Termux:X11 + Accessibility is the nuclear option — and in this case, the *correct* one. We don’t need Tampermonkey, we don’t need headless, we just need a **real visible browser that solves Cloudflare once**. After that, we scrape the `cf_clearance` cookie and the session token from the SQLite profile, then use `curl_cffi` for all subsequent calls. No repeat challenges.

---

## 1. Launch Chromium on X11

Make sure Termux:X11 is running and the display is set, then:

```bash
export DISPLAY=:1
mkdir -p ~/browser-data-mistral

chromium-browser --user-data-dir=$HOME/browser-data-mistral \
  --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check \
  https://chat.mistral.ai &
```

Log in manually via the Mistral web UI, then close the browser when done.

---

## 2. Extract cookies (including `cf_clearance` and session)

Use the exact same SQLite cookie extractor we already wrote:

```bash
python3 ~/multi-ai-cli/harvesters/extract_mistral_cookies.py
```

Check what we got:

```bash
python3 -c "
import json, os
p = os.path.expanduser('~/.multi-ai-tokens/mistral_cookies.json')
data = json.load(open(p))
for c in data:
    if 'cf_' in c['name'] or 'session' in c['name'].lower():
        print(c['name'], c['value'][:50])
"
```

---

## 3. Use the cookies to get a Bearer token

Now that we have `cf_clearance`, we can hit Mistral’s session endpoint without Cloudflare blocking us:

```bash
python3 -c "
from curl_cffi import requests
import json, os

with open(os.path.expanduser('~/.multi-ai-tokens/mistral_cookies.json')) as f:
    cookies = json.load(f)

s = requests.Session(impersonate='chrome110')
for c in cookies:
    s.cookies.set(c['name'], c['value'], domain=c['domain'], path=c.get('path', '/'))
s.headers['User-Agent'] = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Android 14; Mobile; rv:151.0) Gecko/151.0 Firefox/151.0'

r = s.get('https://chat.mistral.ai/api/auth/session')
print('Status:', r.status_code)
if r.ok:
    data = r.json()
    print('Session data:', json.dumps(data, indent=2)[:300])
    # Save token if present
    token = data.get('token') or data.get('accessToken')
    if token:
        open(os.path.expanduser('~/.multi-ai-tokens/mistral_token.txt'), 'w').write(token)
        print('Token saved')
else:
    print('Body:', r.text[:400])
"
```

If this gives us a Bearer token, we’re done. Mistral will be driven like DeepSeek — token in `Authorization` header, no further browser needed. I’ll harden the backend to use that token, and the whole bridge/Tampermonkey path becomes optional backup.
